<problem>
For a nonempty finite poset $S$, a linear extension is a total order on its underlying set that extends its partial order. Its order dimension $\dim S$ is the least positive integer $t$ for which there are linear extensions $L_1,\ldots,L_t$ such that $x\le_S y$ if and only if $x\le_{L_i}y$ for every $i$.

For each positive integer $k$, write $[k]=\{1,\ldots,k\}$. Let $\lambda(k)$ be the number of inclusion-maximal intersecting families of subsets of $[k]$: a family $\mathcal F$ is intersecting when $A\cap B\ne\varnothing$ for all $A,B\in\mathcal F$, including $A=B$, and it is inclusion-maximal when no proper larger family of subsets of $[k]$ is intersecting.

Fix an integer $d\ge8$ and put $M_d=\lambda(d-1)+1$. Let $Q_d$ be the poset consisting of all one-element and two-element subsets of $[M_d]$, ordered by inclusion. For a nonempty finite poset $P$, order $P\times Q_d$ by $(p,A)\le(p',A')$ exactly when $p\le_P p'$ and $A\subseteq A'$.

Let $F(d)$ be the supremum of $\dim(P\times Q_d)-\dim P$ as $P$ ranges over all nonempty finite posets with $\dim P\ge3$. Determine $F(d)$ exactly for every integer $d\ge8$.
</problem>

131	\[
132	v\notin e\quad\Longrightarrow\quad

134	\tag{9}
135	\]

137	\[
138	D(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)\cap D(\mathcal F,\mathcal H)\ne\varnothing,

153	\[
154	\Phi_j(p_1,p_2,q)

157	\tag{10}
158	\]

163	Thus \(\Phi\) is an order embedding into a product of \(k+1\) chains, proving (7).

167	P\times Q_d

172	\dim(P\times Q_d)

174	\]

181	## 3. The lower bound
182	
183	First,
184	\[
185	\dim Q_d\geq d.
186	\tag{12}
187	\]

190	
191	Suppose \(L_1,\ldots,L_t\) realize \(Q(N)\). Restrict them to the vertices and put
192	\[
193	E(v,u)=\{i:v>u\text{ in }L_i\}.
194	\]

196	
197	Extend this intersecting family to a maximal intersecting family \(\mathcal A_v\) on \([t]\). If \(u\ne v\), then \(E(v,u)\) and \(E(u,v)\) are complementary, so they cannot both belong to one intersecting family. Thus
198	\[
199	\mathcal A_v\ne\mathcal A_u.
200	\]
201	It follows that
202	\[
203	N\leq\lambda(t).
204	\tag{13}
205	\]
206	
207	If \(Q_d\) had a realizer with at most \(d-1\) extensions, repeat extensions to obtain exactly \(d-1\). Equation (13) would contradict
208	\[
209	N=\lambda(d-1)+1.
210	\]
211	This proves (12). The construction in Section 2 also gives \(\dim Q_d\leq d\), so in fact \(\dim Q_d=d\).
212	
213	Take \(P=S_3\), of dimension three. The standard-example product inequality (1) gives
214	\[
215	\dim(S_3\times Q_d)\geq3+d-2=d+1.
216	\]
217	Hence
218	\[
219	\dim(S_3\times Q_d)-\dim S_3\geq d-2.
220	\tag{14}
221	\]
222	Together, (11) and (14) prove the answer.
223	
224	## 4. Executable checks
225	
226	The following Python does actual exhaustive enumeration and certificate checking. It:
227	
228	* enumerates all maximal intersecting families through \(k=6\);
229	* counts all \(1\,422\,564\) families for \(k=7\), checking the extra-word and label-choice assertions for every one;

241	    ps = [(a, U ^ a) for a in range(1, U) if a < (U ^ a)]
